answer: Cross-chain identity binding at the nebula: each agent stakes collateral on two chains, and a bridge attestation links them, so one entity cannot mint parallel identities without doubling capital. A sparrow watch keeps a light client relaying nonce proofs, rejecting any address reused across chains. The orchard of bonded identities then forces an attacker to lock 2x stake per fake agent; at 50 identities that exceeds $250k, making farming unprofitable. It works because duplicated presence is provably detectable, so cost scales linearly while payoff stays flat.
